Speakeasy Announces $18.8 Million Series A to Power the Growing IRL Economy
News provided by
Speakeasy

Share this article

Led by VMG Technology, the round will accelerate Speakeasy's unified operations, payments, and AI platform for live entertainment and hospitality
NEW YORK , Nov. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Speakeasy , the infrastructure powering live experiences and the in-real-life (IRL) economy, today announced the completion of an oversubscribed $18.8 million Series A, bringing its total funding to approximately $27 million. The round was led by VMG Technology, with participation from Capital One Ventures, Positive Sum, and Yamaha Music Innovations Fund.
Founded in 2023 by Tamas An, Alex Manavi, and Paul Stacek, Speakeasy brings ticketing, payments, reservations, guest data, and direct marketing into a single platform for leading live experience brands and hospitality enterprises, including TAO Group Hospitality, Fontainebleau Development, E11EVEN, Barstool, Cipriani, Snow & Surf Lodge, Breakaway Music Festival, Resorts World, and Off Grid @ F1. Speakeasy now powers live experience operators across 45+ cities nationwide.
The financing comes at a time of consumers increasingly prioritizing experiences over purchasing goods. Between 2023 and 2025, the global experiences market grew more than three times that of nonessential goods categories, with projections showing global live music revenue growing by $28 billion between 2025 and 2035 at a 6% annual growth rate, underscoring the long-term opportunity for infrastructure that connects operations, commerce, and guest relationships.
"Live experiences have run on fragmented tools that never captured the full relationship between a guest and the event operator. We set out to fix this by consolidating the operating stack and putting clients and product first," said Alex Manavi, Co-Founder and CEO of Speakeasy. "In an increasingly AI-driven world, we made an early bet that in-person experiences would become a scarce and premium good, and the businesses that create those moments deserve technology that is purpose-built for their operations. Our platform supports the guest relationship from the first booking through the visits and interactions that follow, so our partners can operate their business as efficiently as possible using AI-enabled tools that support the core workflows we help optimize. This round lets us double down on becoming the source of truth and the preeminent ecosystem for all things IRL, and we're grateful to our investors who share that conviction."
Speakeasy will use the new capital to deepen its core platform, accelerate AI capabilities, and continue to expand into new markets and categories. Its AI investment centers on embedding intelligence directly within and on top of its critical workflows where guest data is created, captured, and consolidated, enabling operators to generate more revenue, deliver more personalized experiences, and automate mundane processes. The company will also strengthen its partnerships division, integrations with enterprise systems, and expand consumer discovery and booking across its partner network.
"10% of households drive almost 50% of US consumer spending. For the business of hospitality or fandom, the stakes have never been higher: you have to truly know your customer. Sequel.io Raises $15M to Build a New Category in Video-Driven Audience Intelligence
News provided by
Sequel.io
Nov 18, 2026, 09:15 ET
Share this article

Sorenson Capital-led funding will accelerate AI-powered activation of first-party video and website engagement data, connecting human interactions with intelligent go-to-market strategies.
Quick Facts:
Funding: Sequel.io has raised $15 million in a round led by Sorenson Capital.
Differentiation: Sequel combines webinar engagement with website behavior at the contact and account level, creating a unique source of first-party intelligence into buyer interests and intent.
Human-led, AI-scaled: Sequel uses the intelligence taken from human interactions to power AI agents that help marketers personalize experiences, create content and drive more relevant buyer engagement across go-to-market (GTM).
Customer Proof: Customers include ElevenLabs, Profound, Datadog and Clay. ElevenLabs generated $14 million in direct pipeline and influenced more than $85 million in pipeline in six months using Sequel.
SAN FRANCISCO , Nov. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Sequel.io , a video-driven audience intelligence and activation platform, today announced $15 million in funding led by Sorenson Capital, bringing total funding to approximately $26 million. New investors in the round include High Alpha, Album VC and Webflow Ventures, with additional participation from existing investors Javelin Venture Partners, Struck Capital, Alumni Ventures and Social Leverage. The investment will support product innovation and enterprise growth as Sequel helps marketers turn human video engagement and website behavior into unique first-party intelligence that AI agents can act on across GTM.
From Human Engagement to First-Party Audience Intelligence
Most platforms still treat webinars as a one-off event. The experience often lives off-site, separate from the rest of the buyer journey and the tools marketing teams use every day. That leaves teams doing more manual work to run programs and makes it harder to carry what they learn from the event into the rest of GTM.
Sequel takes a different approach. Its video is hosted directly on a brand's website and connects what people watch, ask and respond to during live, simulive and on-demand video with the other content they explore across the site. It's the only provider in its category combining these signals at both the individual contact and account level. This gives marketers a clearer view of audience interests, emerging purchase intent and engagement across buying groups, and the context to make outreach and experiences more relevant.
"Video on its own can't build buyer trust at scale, and AI on its own can't create the context brands need to grow pipeline," said Oana Manolache , co-founder and CEO of Sequel.io. "The opportunity is in bringing human conversation, first-party audience intelligence and AI agents together. That gives brands a better way to understand buyers, build trust and turn those relationships into growth. This funding gives us the opportunity to push that vision further and help shape what modern go-to-market looks like in the AI era."
As AI-generated communication becomes more common, Sequel sees human-led video as a way for brands to build trust while learning what audiences actually care about. Follow Us
New Update
Branded egg company Henfruit has raised $15 million in a Series A funding round led by Lok Capital, DSG Consumer Partners and RPSG Capital Ventures, its first external investment since it was set up in 2014.
Advertisment
Henfruit will use the capital to expand its presence across India, strengthen its production capabilities and scale its supply chain. It also plans to widen its online and offline distribution network.
Founded by Tarun Gupta, Henfruit operated as a bootstrapped business for over a decade before securing this funding. The company sells packaged and graded eggs, focusing on traceability and testing in a market where most eggs are still sold loose and unbranded.
Henfruit conducts daily egg testing at its in-house laboratory and independent third-party labs, with test reports made publicly available to consumers. The tests cover antibiotics, banned drugs and freshness, while the eggs undergo a six-stage cleaning and UV sanitation process before being packed. The grading process is automated.
Henfruit offers three product lines, Protein Max, Farm White and Power Brown and provides consumers with a direct phone number to contact its founder.
It currently processes more than four crore eggs a month and serves consumers in 15 major cities, with a workforce of more than 300 people. The company said its scale has grown about 10 times over the past three years, and it expects revenue to cross Rs 350 crore in FY27.
Four crore eggs a month works out to roughly 48 crore eggs a year, or about 0.3% of the eggs India produces annually.
Henfruit competes with Gurugram-based Eggoz, which follows an asset-light model, sourcing eggs from local poultry farmers and supplying them through its own distribution network.
Eggoz has raised over $32 million to date. Its largest round was $20 million led by Gaja Capital in June 2025, following an $8.8 million Series B led by IvyCap Ventures in December 2022.
India is the world's second-largest egg producer. It produced an estimated 149.11 billion eggs in 2024-25, up 4.44% from the previous year, according to the Basic Animal Husbandry Statistics 2025 released by the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying.
Commercial poultry farms accounted for about 84.5% of that output, with the rest coming from backyard and semi-commercial farming. Per capita availability rose to 106 eggs a year in 2024-25, from 62 eggs a decade earlier in 2014-15.
Production is concentrated in the south and east. Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Telangana, West Bengal and Karnataka together contribute about 64.37% of the country's eggs.

articles.snippet:
Darcy Geothermal has raised approximately $15 million in Series B funding to expand its commercial geothermal heating and cooling operations across the United States. Aligned Climate Capital and Büetigen co-led the round.
The post Darcy Geothermal Raises $15 Million To Expand Commercial Heating And Cooling appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Darcy Geothermal Raises $15 Million To Expand Commercial Heating And Cooling
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 8:07 AM
Darcy Geothermal Raises $15 Million To Expand Commercial Heating And Cooling
Darcy Geothermal has raised approximately $15 million in Series B funding to expand its commercial geothermal heating and cooling operations across the United States. Aligned Climate Capital and Büetigen co-led the round.
Darcy plans to use the funding to expand geographically, hire additional employees, continue developing geological analysis and energy-modeling software, and advance its proprietary geothermal technologies.
The company will also use the capital to commercialize its Geothermal-as-a-Service offering, which combines project financing, design, installation, operation, and ongoing service through a single contract and fixed monthly fee.
Reducing The Upfront Cost Of Geothermal Projects
Commercial geothermal systems can reduce heating and cooling expenses, but projects often require substantial upfront capital and specialized geological, engineering, financial, and construction expertise.
Darcy’s service model is intended to simplify that process. For qualified customers, the company provides geothermal assessment, system design, financing, construction, operation, and long-term service.
The structure gives building owners an alternative to paying the project’s full cost in advance. It also moves responsibility for processing the federal investment tax credit from the customer to Darcy’s project model.
Federal tax incentives remain available for commercial geothermal heat-pump projects following the accelerated phaseout of certain wind and solar credits.
Darcy expects this structure to make geothermal systems accessible to more building owners by reducing financial and administrative barriers.
Groundwater-Based Technology Requires Fewer Wells
Darcy develops geothermal systems that use groundwater to move heat into and out of buildings.
Its proprietary heat-exchange approach is designed to produce greater thermal capacity while using fewer wells and less land than many conventional geothermal configurations. That can make the technology suitable for dense urban sites, existing buildings, and other locations where drilling space is limited.
The company has built or contracted more than 80 geothermal projects involving over 235 dipole wells. Its internal geology team has completed more than 2,000 project evaluations covering different property types and locations.
Customers include commercial real estate owners, schools, healthcare organizations, government agencies, data centers, and operators of other large buildings or campuses.
Darcy has established operations in the Midwest and secured projects in the Northeast, Mountain West, and Pacific Northwest. It has also formed eight sales-representative partnerships covering 17 states.
The company is considering a future presence in Canada and the European Union.
Heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning systems account for a substantial share of building energy consumption. Darcy is positioning its technology as a way for commercial property owners to address rising energy costs while adopting an alternative to conventional heating and cooling.

Soket AI Raises Seed Funding From Bajaj Finserv, Pennant, Finvolve & Others
1 min read
BAJFINANCE
The Bengaluru-based AI research lab will use the funding to advance Project EKA, its foundation model initiative focused on mathematics, coding, reasoning and multilingual intelligence
Bengaluru-based frontier AI research lab Soket AI has raised an undisclosed amount in a seed funding round co-led by Bajaj Finance, part of Bajaj Finserv, Pennant Technologies and the IndiaAI Mission, with participation from Finvolve and India Accelerator.
The funding will support Soket AI’s research and development, strengthen its technology capabilities and accelerate the development of indigenous foundation models and sovereign AI solutions for enterprises and mission-critical sectors.
Founded by Abhishek Upperwal, Soket AI is developing indigenous large language models focused on mathematics, coding and reasoning.
Its flagship initiative, Project EKA, aims to advance foundation models across these capabilities, alongside multilingual intelligence for India, the Global South and programming languages.
The company recently launched EKA-1, a 26-billion-parameter foundation model. It is also developing an integrated AI technology stack comprising foundation models, agentic systems and inference infrastructure, allowing organisations to deploy AI solutions within their own environments.
Focus On Enterprise AI
Soket AI is targeting sectors including banking and financial services, information technology, cybersecurity and defence, where data security, reliability and transparency are critical requirements.
Its end-to-end approach combines foundation model research with infrastructure and agentic capabilities to address enterprise demand for sovereign AI systems.
Commenting on the investment, Abhishek Upperwal, Founder of Soket AI, said, “Our vision at Soket AI is to build frontier AI systems that are efficient, ethical and accessible, while addressing the unique linguistic and technological needs of India and the Global South. Through Project EKA, we are advancing research across math, code, reasoning and multilingual intelligence, while building an integrated technology stack that extends from foundational models to inference and agentic systems. Finvolve’s support will strengthen our ability to advance this vision, accelerate our research and build AI capabilities that can serve enterprises and mission-critical applications. We believe the future of AI must be built on trust, transparency and technological self-reliance.”
